source: Post-audit enacted laws and substantive 2026 codification registry
description: Publication metadata for authenticated newer enactments, their verified amendment or statutory-note anchors, and subsequent repeal overrides. Note targets are editorial placements, not claims that the cited section's enacted text was rewritten.

actions.description: National-security eligibility provisions are classified to 50 U.S.C. §§ 5001–5007.
Commerce, trade, intellectual-property, and labor transfer provisions are classified to 15 U.S.C. §§ 10001–10011.
Conflict-of-interest provisions are consolidated into 18 U.S.C. § 205 as new subsections (k)–(n).
Commissioned-service staffing and continuity provisions are classified to 5 U.S.C. §§ 2501–2504.
Whistleblower and oversight protections are classified to 5 U.S.C. §§ 2308–2314.
Express repeals and transition, savings, severability, and effective-date provisions are retained as statutory history or notes where appropriate.

laws.title: Metropolitan Police Department Public Safety and Property Reform Act

actions.description: Permanent MPD public-safety and property-authority provisions are classified to 40 U.S.C. §§ 9701–9716.
Short-title, severability, and effective-date provisions are retained as notes at 40 U.S.C. § 9701.
Federal law-enforcement communications and coordination provisions are classified to 6 U.S.C. §§ 1801–1815.
Short-title, severability, and effective-date provisions are retained as notes at 6 U.S.C. § 1801.

laws.title: United States Capitol Police Reform and Accountability Act

actions.description: Permanent Capitol Police organization, governance, jurisdiction, protective-service, enforcement, use-of-force, oversight, access, emergency, political-neutrality, and penalty provisions are classified to 2 U.S.C. §§ 7001–7019.

The Act expressly repeals the Uniformed Capitol Police Act of 2023 and the United States Capitol Police Technical Corrections Act, terminates authority dependent solely on those enactments, and supersedes inconsistent continuing law, rule, regulation, or order. Existing archived law identities are preserved where the historical archive contains conflicting public-law numbering.

actions.treatment: short-title, severability, rule-of-construction, and effective-date notes
actions.description: Short-title, severability, rule-of-construction, and effective-date/transition provisions are retained as statutory notes at 2 U.S.C. § 7001.

actions.effect_label: Amendment to an earlier public law
actions.description: Amends §§ 5–6 of Pub. L. 16-116, leaving U.S. Special Operations Command as the only combatant command established by that Act and changing the reporting and operational-command rules. Definitions reference Title 10 but do not amend the cited Code provisions.

laws.title: Federal Aviation Administration Continuity and Restricted Airspace Act

actions.effect_label: Direct Code amendments — recorded in note
actions.treatment: controlling amendment note pending structural consolidation
actions.description: Directly amends 49 U.S.C. § 106 to place FAA under joint DHS/NASA administration, define the Administrator and supervisory authorities, and provide conforming changes. The amendment is recorded at its actual target without rewriting unrelated provisions or guessing subsection nesting.

actions.effect_label: New NASA airspace authority — statutory note
actions.description: Adds NASA facility airspace powers after 51 U.S.C. § 20113 in chapter 201; § 8 refers to 51 U.S.C. § 20113A, although the insertion instruction in § 6 does not give the new section an explicit numbered heading. Recorded at § 20113 pending that structural reconciliation.

actions.effect_label: Direct Code amendment — recorded in note
actions.treatment: controlling amendment note pending structural consolidation
actions.description: Adds mandatory permanent restricted flight areas at the White House Complex, Capitol complex, Joint Base Moore and specified security areas to 49 U.S.C. § 40103.

actions.effect_label: Direct Code amendment — recorded in note
actions.treatment: controlling amendment note pending structural consolidation
actions.description: Adds airspace-restriction civil enforcement, grounding, administrative remedies and criminal referrals to 49 U.S.C. § 46301.
The Act's definitions, construction rules, severability and effective date are preserved in the original enactment; their incidental Code citations are not treated as amended sections.

actions.effect_label: Amendment to Pub. L. 42-273 — recorded in Code note
actions.description: Amends § 4(b) of Pub. L. 42-273: the Director shall be appointed by the President after consultation with the Secretary of Homeland Security. Recorded beside the corresponding § 4 codification at 6 U.S.C. § 1803; no unrelated sections are amended.

laws.title: Please Help We Don't Have Enough Judges Act

actions.description: Restates § 103 of Pub. L. 30-222 to permit the Chief Justice to appoint no fewer than one district judge to the FISA Court for renewable six-month terms. This amends the prior public law, not an expressly identified Code section; recorded at the prior Act's Title 50 statutory-note anchor.

Requires an enacted joint resolution before a covered military service or the D.C. National Guard can be activated or deactivated, including constructively; preserves the President's command and operational authority. The Act defines covered forces by reference to 10 U.S.C. § 101 but does not amend that section.

actions.effect_label: Express repeal of an earlier public law
actions.description: Expressly repeals Pub. L. 26-188 (Departmental Reports Act) in full. The earlier enactment is marked repealed in the publication registry.

actions.effect_label: New continuing reporting and penalty requirements
actions.description: Creates monthly congressional reporting duties for State, Defense, Justice, Homeland Security and the Director of National Intelligence, subject to permitted withholding and penalties. The Act references 5 U.S.C. § 101 for definitions but does not amend that section.

actions.effect_label: Short title, severability and effective date
actions.description: Takes effect on the first full calendar month after enactment; the short title and severability provisions do not modify any Code section.
Pub. L. 44-280, § 3(e), expressly repealed the Departmental Reports Act (Pub. L. 26-188). Historical codifications are not operative by virtue of the former Act.
